name: Samarokena
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog shows no descriptive works; apparently only survey wordlists for this TAR-area language

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane, Mark Donohue & Felix Ma. 2002. Survey report of the north coast of Irian Jaya. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-078. Dallas: SIL International. 10 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 4.3 'Airoran and Samarokena' (p. 8) gives a tentative joint phoneme chart for Airoran and Samarokena and remarks only that 'there are also some instances of a stressed schwa appearing in the data, suggesting that schwa might also be a contrastive sound'; it does not say where stress falls. downloaded from the the Internet Archive copy of the old sil.org PDF (live sil.org returns not reachable by automated download).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid sama1240 and its reference listing (11 references: Stokhof 1983; Le Roux n.d. Woordenlijsten; Smits & Voorhoeve 1998; Voorhoeve 1975; Galis 1955; Clouse, Donohue & Ma 2002; van der Leeden 1954, 1956; Koentjaraningrat 1963; Du Buy 1955)
sources.note: Bibliographic record only; every reference is typed wordlist / overview / ethnographic / minimal; no grammar, sketch or phonology exists for the language.
Stub: 'poorly documented Papuan language'; villages Karfasia, Maseb, Samarkena, Tamaya; classification notes (Wurm 1975, Ross 2005, Donohue 2002). Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Stokhof, W. A. L. (ed.). 1983. Holle Lists: Vocabularies in languages of Indonesia, Vol. 5/2: Irian Jaya: Papuan languages, Northern languages, Central Highlands languages. Pacific Linguistics D-53. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Contains the 'Tomajo' Holle list 143a (pp. 43-46), the Samarokena list used by ASJP (SAMAROKENA_TOMAYO); colonial-era vocabulary only, no stress marking and no statement about stress.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Entry 71 SAMAROKENA (Tamaja), p. 38 (villages, ±400 speakers, sources Van der Leeden 1955, Galis 1955, unpublished U4) and a 40-item Anceaux wordlist column '71. SAMAROKENA (Ac)' on p. 105; no stress marks, no statement on stress.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of Northwest New Guinea. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 433-568. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher
sources.note: Handbook chapter covering the Kwerba (Greater Kwerba) family; may summarise phonology, possibly with a family-level remark on stress; unknown whether Samarokena is treated beyond classification.
sources.venue: The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide

sources.citation: Smits, Leo & C. L. Voorhoeve. 1998. The J. C. Anceaux collection of wordlists of Irian Jaya languages B: Non-Austronesian (Papuan) languages (Part II). Irian Jaya Source Materials 10, Series B no. 4. Leiden/Jakarta: DSALCUL/IRIS.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The fullest Samarokena wordlist in print (Anceaux's field transcription, the 'Ac' source of Voorhoeve 1975); Anceaux's transcriptions sometimes carry accent marks, which would be the only primary evidence on stress placement, though the volume has no phonological statement.

sources.citation: Galis, Klaas Wilhelm. 1955. Talen en dialecten van Nederlands Nieuw-Guinea. Tijdschrift Nieuw-Guinea 16: 109-118, 134-145, 161-178.

sources.note: Earliest survey with a Samarokena wordlist (cited by Voorhoeve 1975 as N, Wl; S); a Dutch colonial word list might mark accent, but is unlikely to state a rule.
